iconicAnchor.label: Relief printing from movable type and image matrices on a hand or proof press
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Library of Congress definition identifies the central mechanism: a letterpress print is made with a relief matrix such as metal or wood type, photoengraving, linocut, photopolymer, or wood engraving.

sources.title: Glossary — The Russell Maret Artist Book Collection and Archive
supports: Letterpress uses raised relief matrices including movable type, linocut, photopolymer plates, and wood engraving.
The medium's visual grammar can include both typographic and image matrices rather than only historical metal type.

sources.title: Wooden Hand Presses
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
supports: Traditional type-printing presses use a bed, platen, and pressure mechanism to bring an inked forme and paper together.
Press construction and available pressure constrain sheet size, setup, and the physical production sequence.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches letterpress ink, paper, typographic, craft signal, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/letterpress-print/reference-01.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
